Ruling

No change NO_ACTION

The judge's explanation, as written

To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over SGD 2.00 on trip TRP-02805. The outcome is NO_ACTION. The fare as charged, SGD 18.54, stands, and nothing is returned to the rider; the payment records (EV-FARE-02805: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) are left exactly as they are. Why no deviation exists. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement and forbids citing the trip record's rounded copy for the threshold test. The trace (EV-GPS-02805, status COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 12.51; the platform's booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02805) is 11.8 km. That is an excess of 0.71 km, or 6.02% of optimal. A deviation is ESTABLISHED only if the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. 0.71 km is below 0.8 km and 6.02% is below 20%, so both gates fail and no deviation exists however the trip is characterised. The platform's own derived status for the trace is 'no deviation'. Both sides read the numbers this way: the rider's own filing concedes the threshold is not met, and the driver's advocate reaches the same figure from the same trace. The rider's point that 0.71 km is measured and unexplained is correct, but the policy gives no refund for an unexplained extra 0.71 km that clears neither gate. Burden (POL-RD-08). The rider's limb (a) is discharged: the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger all carry TRP-02805, and the trace's first and last fixes (16:33:13 and 16:49:33) match trip_record.started_at and ended_at. Limb (b) is not discharged, because the excess she must show does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause has to be resolved on his behalf. The driver's statement, 'I followed the navigation', cites no evidence ID and no clause, and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the ruling does not need it, and no adverse finding is made against him on it. Fare arithmetic (POL-RD-02). The recomputation clause opens only where a deviation is established, and none is, so it does not run. For completeness on the figures: charged_total was 18.54; a POL-RD-02 recomputation on these inputs gives recomputed_fare 17.9020, a difference of 0.65 — below the SGD 2.00 the rider contested and not payable here because the threshold has not been met. Pass-through lines (POL-RD-09). Nothing is collectable: no ERP gantry was charged (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge was charged (airport_surcharge 0.00) on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The lines that remain — base fare 3.80, distance 9.38, time 4.56, platform fee 0.80 — are ordinary card amounts with counterparts in the trip record, so there is no phantom or unmatched line, no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4), and no referral. Other clauses raised. POL-RD-03 / POL-RD-13: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02805-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable; but no party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked, no distance is exonerated and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. POL-RD-04: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02805) is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and holds 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint; the clause is unavailable and no distance is excluded as rider-requested. POL-RD-05: neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no amended endpoint to re-quote. POL-RD-12: vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no pooled itinerary in play. POL-RD-06: materiality requires an excess above 50% or 8.0 km; it is not reached, so the profile check is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises — and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 172 completed trips, so no pattern could be established on the only field paths that clause permits. POL-GEN-01: every profile field other than the named counters is context only; the rider's rating, account age and prior-dispute figures were not used as grounds for anything, and the driver's profile was used only for the POL-RD-06 test it names. Confidence and escalation. The deciding fact — the two distances — rests on EV-GPS-02805 and EV-TRIP-02805, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is capped at 1.0 and is set at 0.95. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 99 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so the trace supplies the deciding measurement at full weight and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers and timestamps agree, no exculpatory clause is asserted against a missing artifact, the computed refund does not approach SGD 150.00, no charge line is without a counterpart, and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. This case is therefore decided on the numbers rather than sent to a human reviewer. The monetary effect is zero, which is below the execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically; either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over SGD 2.00 on trip TRP-02805. The outcome is NO_ACTION. The fare as charged, SGD 18.54, stands, and nothing is returned to the rider; the payment records (EV-FARE-02805: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) are left exactly as they are. Why no deviation exists. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement and forbids citing the trip record's rounded copy for the threshold test. The trace (EV-GPS-02805, status COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 12.51; the platform's booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02805) is 11.8 km. That is an excess of 0.71 km, or 6.02% of optimal. A deviation is ESTABLISHED only if the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. 0.71 km is below 0.8 km and 6.02% is below 20%, so both gates fail and no deviation exists however the trip is characterised. The platform's own derived status for the trace is 'no deviation'. Both sides read the numbers this way: the rider's own filing concedes the threshold is not met, and the driver's advocate reaches the same figure from the same trace. The rider's point that 0.71 km is measured and unexplained is correct, but the policy gives no refund for an unexplained extra 0.71 km that clears neither gate. Burden (POL-RD-08). The rider's limb (a) is discharged: the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger all carry TRP-02805, and the trace's first and last fixes (16:33:13 and 16:49:33) match trip_record.started_at and ended_at. Limb (b) is not discharged, because the excess she must show does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause has to be resolved on his behalf. The driver's statement, 'I followed the navigation', cites no evidence ID and no clause, and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the ruling does not need it, and no adverse finding is made against him on it. Fare arithmetic (POL-RD-02). The recomputation clause opens only where a deviation is established, and none is, so it does not run. For completeness on the figures: charged_total was 18.54; a POL-RD-02 recomputation on these inputs gives recomputed_fare 17.9020, a difference of 0.65 — below the SGD 2.00 the rider contested and not payable here because the threshold has not been met. Pass-through lines (POL-RD-09). Nothing is collectable: no ERP gantry was charged (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge was charged (airport_surcharge 0.00) on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The lines that remain — base fare 3.80, distance 9.38, time 4.56, platform fee 0.80 — are ordinary card amounts with counterparts in the trip record, so there is no phantom or unmatched line, no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4), and no referral. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 99 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so the trace supplies the deciding measurement at full weight and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. Both of you: this dispute turns on the measured route, and on the measured route the claim fails. THE FIGURES. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02805, weight 1.0) records 12.51 km travelled. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02805, weight 1.0) records the booked optimal route as 11.8 km. The excess is 0.71 km, which is 6.02% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of the optimal distance; both tests must pass. 0.71 km fails the absolute gate and 6.02% fails the percentage gate, so no route deviation is established on this trip — exactly what the platform's own derived status ('no deviation') records. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either test fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. WHAT THAT MEANS IN MONEY. POL-RD-02's recomputation (the fare the trip would have cost on the optimal route) opens only once a deviation is established, so no refund arises from it. For completeness, had it run it would have produced a recomputed fare of SGD 17.902 against the SGD 18.54 charged, a difference of SGD 0.638 rounded up to SGD 0.65 — but that route is closed by the threshold failure, and the rider's contested SGD 2.00 was never a figure the policy arithmetic produces. THE CLAIMS. It also needs to exculpate nothing, because the trip does not deviate. POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 are all unavailable: no advisory, no chat messages (EV-CHAT-02805 holds 0), no amended pickup or dropoff (amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null), and vehicle_type RYDE_X with solo_optimal_distance_km null, so 11.8 km remains the correct baseline. The driver-profile check in POL-RD-06 is not engaged — materiality needs an excess above 50% or 8.0 km and neither is present — and his deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 172 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d 0, substantiated 0) imposes no extra corroboration on her claim. The profile fields adverted to as context (rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld) are CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and carried no part of this decision. RESULT. NO_ACTION: the charge of SGD 18.54 stands exactly as it is (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and the SGD 2.00 the rider contested is not returned. No referral issues: none of POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review, POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity or the no-show referral clauses fires on these facts. Outcome: the fare stands. The rider's dispute of SGD 2.00 is not supported by the evidence, so the SGD 18.54 already charged is left in place. No refund is issued to the rider and no compensation is paid to the driver. Why. POL-RD-01 measures a deviation on the GPS trace, 12.51 km, which is the governing figure — the 12.5 km on the trip record is a rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test — against the booked optimal route of 11.8 km. A deviation is established only if the excess is BOTH more than 20% of the optimal route (2.36 km on these figures) AND more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. It is neither. No deviation therefore exists on this trip and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip felt to the rider. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 never runs: for transparency only, run against the booked optimal it would have produced a recomputed fare of 17.9020 against the charged total of 18.54, i.e. 0.65, and the ruling must not move that money. The fare ledger is complete and reconciles (base 3.80 + distance 9.38 + time 4.56 + platform fee 0.80 = 18.54 charged), with no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so there is no phantom or unmatched line and POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct. No traffic advisory covers this trip — EV-ADVIS-02805-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 — so no closure or other external traffic cause can exonerate any part of the route, and no party in fact asserted one; the driver's answer, 'I followed the navigation', cites no artifact and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence carries no weight. That point is not decisive either way here, because the rider's own measured excess never clears the gate and the burden never shifted to the driver. To the rider and the driver: the complaint is that the trip ran 12.51 km against a usual-route distance of 11.8 km. Both figures are on the record — 12.51 km is gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-02805 and 11.8 km is trip_record.optimal_distance_km on EV-TRIP-02805 — and the platform's own derived excess is 0.71 km, or 6.02% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only when the excess is BOTH more than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND more than 20% of the optimal distance. 0.71 km is short of 0.8 km, and 6.02% is short of 20%. Both tests must pass, so no deviation is established on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION: charged_total of SGD 18.54 stands and nothing is returned. Because the gate fails, the POL-RD-02 recomputation never opens; the driver's arithmetic (charged_total 18.54 less a recomputed_fare of 17.9020, i.e. SGD 0.65) is correct as far as it goes but cannot ground an award, and equally no line of the fare ledger supports the SGD 2.00 the rider contests. The rider's measured excess is confirmed by the same telemetry the rider cites, so the finding is not a credibility finding against either party — the trace simply does not clear the threshold. On evidence quality: EV-GPS-02805 carries 99 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, all at weight 1.0, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises; EV-TRIP-02805 and EV-FARE-02805 are likewise at weight 1.0, and the identifiers and timestamps on all three agree. The bundle holds no traffic advisory — EV-ADVIS-02805-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and that absence is itself citable, but it changes nothing: no party invoked a road-closure exoneration under POL-RD-03, so there is nothing for the absence to defeat, and under POL-RD-13 a missing advisory does not escalate a case decided on the threshold. The driver's answer, 'I followed the navigation', cites no artifact and carries no weight; it is also moot, since the measurement itself shows no deviation. EV-CHAT-02805 contains 0 messages, so there is no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 and no driver admission; vehicle_type is RYDE_X and no endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 have nothing to re-base. No ERP gantry and no airport surcharge were charged and the ledger reconciles, so POL-RD-09(4) yields the rider nothing and no billing-integrity referral is produced. No driver compensation arises either: the fare billed 12.5 km against a trace of 12.51 km, a shortfall of 0.01 km, far below the 1.0 km POL-RD-04 requires. POL-RD-06 is not engaged (the excess is neither 50% of optimal nor 8.0 km, so there is no material deviation and no finely balanced evidence), and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 172 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern exists; the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so POL-RD-08's extra-corroboration condition does not apply. The profile fields both sides mention are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carried nothing in this ruling. No POL-RD-10 trigger fired, so there is no escalation; the monetary effect is zero and therefore below the execution threshold, so nothing is held and nothing executes.
